title: SoP5/15: The PRA's methodologies for setting Pillar 2 capital - January 2026 Update

source.name: Bank of England / Prudential Regulation Authority

summary: The PRA published an updated Statement of Policy (SoP 5/15) detailing its methodologies for setting Pillar 2 capital requirements for UK-regulated banks, building societies, designated investment firms, and holding companies, effective 1 January 2027. The document outlines assessment approaches for credit risk, market risk, operational risk, counterparty credit risk, credit concentration risk, interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB), pension obligation risk, and group risk, comparing standardised approach (SA) risk weights against IRB benchmarks. The document accompanies PS1/26, PS2/26, and PS4/26.
key_points: Pillar 2A methodologies cover credit risk, market risk, operational risk, counterparty credit risk, credit concentration risk, IRRBB, pension obligation risk, and group risk for PRA-regulated firms (excluding SDDTs).

Credit risk assessment methodology compares firms' SA risk weights to IRB risk-weight benchmarks at portfolio level, with separate benchmarks for mortgages (14 LTV bands), credit cards, corporates, sovereigns, and institutions.

The PRA may apply additional Pillar 2A capital where SA underestimates risk (e.g., zero risk-weighted sovereigns) but does not apply this where IRB model deficiencies cause shortfalls, instead requiring model remediation.
Benchmarks are calculated based on both unexpected and expected losses (Table A1) and unexpected losses only (Table A2, for IFRS firms where ECL may be covered by Pillar 1 capital).
Pillar 2B section covers the PRA buffer's purpose, determination, and relationship to CRD buffers, including approach to weak governance and risk management.
Effective date is 1 January 2027, updating the October 2025 version, and accompanied by PS1/26, PS2/26, and PS4/26 policy statements.
The document does not apply to Small Domestic Deposit Takers (SDDTs), which have a separate SoP 5/25.
why_it_matters: UK bank capital requirement methodologies directly affect how much capital lenders must hold against credit risk, market risk, and other exposures. Changes to these methodologies (effective 2027) could affect risk-weighted assets and ultimately lending capacity or cost of capital for affected institutions. For market participants, this affects assessment of UK banking sector capital adequacy and potential balance sheet constraints.
market_structure_context: The document covers IRRBB (interest rate risk in the banking book) methodology for bank capital adequacy purposes - this is internal bank risk management for balance sheet hedging, not market structure in the sense of trading venue mechanics or market operations. Banking sector structural risk management is distinct from financial market microstructure.
